data.title: Naming staff for a contract not yet won is an adjudicated practice (GAO, ASRC Federal Data Solutions)
data.summary: Hiring against unsigned funding is regular enough in US federal procurement to have its own body of decided law. To sustain a protest that an awardee performed an impermissible "bait and switch", GAO requires a protester to show "the awardee either knowingly or negligently represented that it would rely on specific personnel that it did not have a reasonable basis to expect to furnish during contract performance", that the agency relied on the misrepresentation, and that the reliance "had a material effect on the evaluation results". The test presupposes the practice it polices: bidders name real candidates for roles that exist only if the bid wins, and the mechanism is the contingent offer, which the decision distinguishes from an exclusive letter of commitment. What is adjudicated is the representation made to the agency, not what becomes of the candidate: the decision says nothing about whether anyone tells the candidate the funding is conditional, and nothing about what follows a lost bid. It governs US federal contracting and establishes that the arrangement is standard and regulated, not how often it occurs.
data.citation: ASRC Federal Data Solutions, LLC, B-421008.2; B-421008.3 (Comp. Gen. Dec. 2, 2022) (protest sustained). B-421008 is the original protest docket; the sustained decision carries the .2 and .3 numbers.
